issue_context.title: ServiceAntiAffinityPriority as score plugin
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
convert ServiceAntiAffinityPriority to a score plugin
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/571cea0519eef38d77524f4074b3bd31bb7f5091/pkg/scheduler/algorithm_factory.go#L382-L392

**Why is this needed**:
part of #83554

**Additional Notes**
#84297 as an example for converting a custom predicate to a filter plugin. The work required here should be very similar to it.

/sig scheduling
/cc @ahg-g
/priority important-soon
/help
comments: Plugin name should be ServiceAffinity (so we will have a Score for this one and Filter for CheckServiceAffinity predicate under the same plugin).

/milestone v1.17

@notpad any progress on this one?
@ahg-g I am still working on this, will submit a PR tomorrow.
Bug triage for 1.17 here, code freeze is in less then two weeks on Nov. 14 (Thursday). Looks like a PR is underway. If it isn't going to be resolved before then, can we move it out of the milestone?

review_comments: that is why the tests are passing, we are not using New to instantiate the priority.
yeah... I will leave it as is and create a follow up to update the tests - creating a fake SharedInformerFactory is not easy.
We need good documentation explaining why we have this awkward implementation: that we are trying to workaround a v1 API that allows defining only a single label, but multiple custom priorities etc.
Added something, let me know if it look good to you.
Say also that we compensate that by artificially multiplying the weight by the number of labels.
s/host/node everywhere in the file (host is the old name of nodes).
let's not do this since this file is going away soon?

If you remove this, I believe the tests wouldn't pass since only a single priority is actually registered as a prioritizer. This is important for us as a way to revert back to the old scheduling path in case of emergencies.

I think we should change the existing priorities to accept lists as we discussed before, the priority would divide by the number of labels. We still add up the weights to compensate for that.
